feature: UI "hello world" — proves a headless build agent can trigger + read back a real UI test result end to end
notes: Part of Epic #803, UI sibling of #957's hello-world-sql.json. Purpose is NOT to test deep
product logic — it proves the #898 remote-trigger-over-HTTP pipeline (headless POST
/admin/deploy/test-run -> BuildConsole claims + runs the manifest via a live WebView2 ->
POST .../complete -> headless GET .../<runId> poll) can drive a real browser and read back a
genuine pass/fail, so more complex manifests can be trusted.
DESIGN CHANGE (#1016) — captureResponse was ABANDONED here. The endpoint used to be verified by
arming a uiStep captureResponse on '/api/public/hero-headlines' and reading the response body out
of WebView2's content stream. That read (UiTestExecutor.ReadResponseBodyAsync -> GetContentAsync)
proved unreliable: #1011 added a timeout guard so it fails gracefully instead of hanging 21 minutes,
and #1014 moved the read to fire synchronously inside the WebResourceResponseReceived handler, but
neither made GetContentAsync return the body reliably — it still times out on real runs. So this
manifest no longer depends on the WebView2 content stream at all. It splits the old single
captureResponse into two independent, each-reliable halves:
(1) ENDPOINT verification — a plain top-level apiTests GET (HttpTestExecutor, the same proven
HttpClient path apiTests/graphTests already use, no browser involved) asserts the real endpoint
returns status 200, $[0].leadText exists, containsAny the seeded headlines, containsNone the
usual junk sentinels (containsAny/containsNone are scoped to the $[0].leadText string field, not
the whole body, so the legitimate seasonalLabel:null on evergreen rows can't false-fail the
'null' containsNone). It also #877-extracts $[0].leadText into {{heroLeadText}} for the DOM step.
(2) DOM-INTEGRATION verification — step 3's `expect` uses the new #1016 `textContains` field, a
REAL rendered-text assertion (el.innerText/textContent via JS injection). Before #1016, uiStep
`expect` was element-STATE only (visible/hidden/present/absent) and a `textContains` was silently
ignored (see money-path-e2e.json's unused 'ready' and remediation-tracker-e2e.json's note). Now
the hero <h1> (data-testid="hero-headline", added in Home.tsx) is asserted to be visible AND to
genuinely DISPLAY the headline the API served — tying 'the API returned X' to 'the DOM shows X' in
one assertion instead of two disconnected checks.
Why textContains is an ANY-OF array, not just {{heroLeadText}}: useHeroHeadlines.ts SHUFFLES the
fetched headlines and types them one character at a time, so at the instant step 3 runs the <h1>
shows a partial slice of a RANDOM headline, not deterministically $[0]. The array lists
{{heroLeadText}} (the exact value the API served at $[0] — deterministic, and identical to the
component's FALLBACK_HEADLINE shown in the brief pre-fetch window) PLUS the three seeded lead_texts,
so whichever headline the client-side shuffle happens to be typing, its leadText satisfies the
assertion. This proves the DOM renders a genuine API-served headline WITHOUT depending on the
nondeterministic shuffle order. A leadText (~26 chars @ 35ms/char) types out well within the
executor's post-nav (1200ms) + post-step (1000ms) settle, so the only residual flake is the brief
~20ms/char delete transition between headlines — narrow and acceptable for a smoke proof.
The seeded lead_texts (2026-07-19-hero-headlines.sql, row 1 matching useHeroHeadlines.ts's own
FALLBACK_HEADLINE) are admin-editable at runtime via the Hero Headlines screen. If all three seeds
have since been replaced, refresh both the apiTests containsAny list and the textContains statics
against whatever real copy is live; {{heroLeadText}} always tracks whatever the API currently serves.
Step 2 keeps the header CTA button (a stable, code-literal element, not DB content) visible check as
the structural 'did it load' half of the hello-world proof.
